model_output.verdict: A healthcare COO whose resume connects practice growth and operational changes to measurable results.
write_up: This is a strong COO resume! At Lakeshore Dental Partners, you show growth across practices alongside improvements in margin, integration time and hygienist retention. A recruiter can see both the size of your responsibility and what changed under your leadership.

The practice growth line is a model: it names acquisitions and de novo openings alongside the change in same-store EBITDA margin. Your progression at Midwest Physician Alliance, board work and education round out the executive story without getting in its way.

I'd keep the structure and focus on one small improvement: explain how you reduced appointment wait times at Midwest Physician Alliance. Your resume is unlikely to be the thing standing between you and a callback; competition for COO roles will also matter.

cards.line: - Grew the practice count from 38 to 140 through 61 acquisitions and 41 de novo openings while raising same-store EBITDA margin from 17% to 23%
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. You give the recruiter the starting point, the finish and the two routes you used to grow.

cards.line: - Reduced patient wait time to third available appointment from 21 days to 6 across primary care
cards.cannot_tell: The drop in wait time is substantial. What did you change to make it happen?
cards.example: Reduced patient wait time to third available appointment from 21 days to 6 across primary care by [operational changes]
cards.question: What changes did you make to reduce the wait time?

fit.why: Your headline and current role name Chief Operating Officer, and your experience centers on multi-site healthcare operations.

fit.note: Your experience points toward COO roles in multi-site healthcare services. The dental practice growth and earlier physician group work give recruiters two settings in which to place your operating experience.
